title: trace_ids input contract shared by the three /invoke handlers
answers: invoke endpoint returns 500 for non-string trace id
issue detection submits a job for an empty trace list
duplicate trace ids analyzed twice in evaluation job
body:
Invariant: trace_ids on issues/invoke, genai/evaluate/invoke, and scorer/invoke must be a non-empty list of strings, de-duplicated (order-preserving) before any store lookup.
Enforced by: the request schema in each handler (_assert_item_type_string added alongside _assert_array), an explicit empty-list 400 in mlflow/server/handlers.py:_invoke_issue_detection_handler, and an isinstance/str check in _invoke_scorer_handler.
What breaks if skipped: An empty list produces a no-op run and job for issues/invoke; a non-string item reaches the store and returns a 500 rather than a 400; repeated ids are fetched and analyzed twice.
Constraints: Validate before the ownership lookup so the store never sees malformed ids.
applies: Any new invoke-style handler that accepts a list of trace ids for a background job.
says: Submitting an issue detection job with no traces selected creates a useless task.
Triggering background trace evaluation with duplicate trace entries analyzes the same traces twice.
Invalid trace IDs sent to evaluation endpoints return server errors instead of validation messages.
Reject empty trace lists immediately when starting automated trace scoring or assessment runs.
Deduplicate selected traces before launching batch evaluation and issue analysis background jobs.
search: The trace_ids input for issues/invoke, genai/evaluate/invoke, and scorer/invoke background-job endpoints must be a non-empty, deduplicated list of strings validated before store lookups. In mlflow/server/handlers.py, handlers _invoke_issue_detection_handler, _invoke_genai_evaluate_handler, and _invoke_scorer_handler enforce this using _assert_item_type_string, _assert_array, an empty-list 400 check, and isinstance string validation. Skipping validation causes empty lists to spawn no-op jobs, non-string IDs to trigger 500 errors in the store instead of 400 responses, and duplicate IDs to be analyzed repeatedly. This input contract applies to all new invoke-style handlers accepting trace IDs for background jobs.
